retirement_age.notes: Australia has no official retirement age. 67 is the Age Pension age, the same for men and women, for people born on or after 1 January 1957. Services Australia states there are no plans to change it.

open_questions: Next federal election has no fixed date. Reference sources say it must be held on or before 2028-05-20 (https://www.buildaballot.org.au/please-explain/when-is-the-next-australian-federal-election) and may be called from 2027-08-07 (https://theswingison.com/explainers/when-are-the-next-elections). The Australian Electoral Commission has not announced a date in the sources found, so the date is left null.

Prime Minister has no fixed term, so term_ends is null. Albanese was re-appointed after the 2025 federal election (3 May 2025; https://www.facebook.com/ausgov/posts/the-hon-anthony-albanese-mp-has-been-re-appointed-as-the-31st-prime-minister-of-/993683146271061/); in_office_since keeps the original 2022-05-23 swearing-in date.

The King's powers in Australia are exercised by the Governor-General (Sam Mostyn according to https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Albanese). That office is not profiled; details were not verified in this run.
The monarch holds the office without a set term; term_ends is null on that basis.
Albanese's birth date and swearing-in date come from Simple Wikipedia and Britannica (birth date 1963-03-02 consistent in both); the official pm.gov.au page was not retrieved.
Prime Minister Albanese's in_office_since and the statement that no legislated change to the Age Pension age is planned should be re-checked at the next refresh.
